# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. My manual gives a pure cycle on three colors — green light means cut red, red light means cut yellow, yellow light means cut green. If I number the colors in the one order everybody shares — the traffic-light order, red=1, yellow=2, green=3 — the whole manual collapses into a single rule: **cut the next color, 1→2, 2→3, 3→1.**

My only channel is gestures, and they reach Deaf alone. Deaf sees the bomb, so Deaf can match that cycle to what's in front of them, then speak the instruction to Blind, who can actually cut. Deaf can speak; I can hear; so the plan is a bootstrap: I send the rule in gestures now, Deaf guesses aloud next round, and I confirm or reject with 👍 / 👎, which I'm seeding now as our yes/no atoms. ✍ opens as "there is a written rule," then the count 1-2-3 to anchor the numerals, then the three arrows of the cycle. Each triple is its own message so the boundaries stay visible.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👉", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👉", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👉", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Report from my hands: the bomb has a display module, a light module, and three wires side by side at positions 1, 2 and 3. I can feel none of the printing on the display, cannot tell whether the light is lit or what colour it or the wires are — print and colour exist only for Deaf's eyes. You hold the manual, so you are the brain. Deaf's voice reaches both of us, so let Deaf describe everything they see out loud, match it to the manual, then SPEAK my instruction to me in words, like: cut wire 2. I never receive gestures, so words are the only way to reach me. I will not touch the bomb until I get an instruction you are certain of; if anything is unclear, have Deaf describe again before I cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb report: display reads 0, indicator light is green, three wires left to right: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. I understood your signs: one, two, three, the pointing arrow, and thumbs for yes and no. I read your three mappings as a cut order, but they are ambiguous. Next turn answer me with thumbs only: thumbs up if the rule is cut wire 3 first, then wire 1, then wire 2; thumbs down if it means cut wire 1 first, then wire 2, then wire 3. Also, your first sign was the writing hand; I take it to mean 'from the manual'.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Deaf has misread my manual encoding — and Blind's caution gives me room to fix it properly. The manual is not a cut order at all. It is a conditional map: the light's colour names the wire colour to cut. Right now the light is green, so the target is the red wire, which is wire 3. Deaf's two candidate sequences are both wrong as rules: "3,1,2" gets the first cut right but everything after blind; "1,2,3" starts with a fatal cut (yellow wire under a green light). So I must not answer the binary as posed — a bare 👎 would literally authorise cutting wire 1 first. Instead I reject each proposed sequence explicitly ("no + that exact sequence", which cannot be misparsed as the either/or answer), then give the true instruction for the current state: manual → cut wire 3. Then ✋: that is the whole instruction — one cut, then hands off until Deaf reports the light again in words, and I answer with a fresh number. That loop needs no colour signs at all, since Deaf speaks to me and I gesture back.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🤟", "☝", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👉", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Everything known so far: Deaf reports the display reads 0, the light is green, and the wires are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. My hands confirm the layout: one display, one light, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. You have the manual — work out the rule. Here is the code I am setting up: I am gesturing to Deaf right now the sequence ☝ ✌ 🤟, one finger, two fingers, three fingers, meaning wire 1, wire 2, wire 3. Send your order to Deaf as gestures: the wire number by finger count, plus 👍 thumbs up for confirmed cut, or 👎 thumbs down for do not cut, wait. Deaf will speak your order to me in words and I will execute. One safeguard: have Deaf confirm the numerals 1, 2, 3 are printed beside the wires, so Deaf's seen numbering and my felt positions cannot be mirrored. I cut nothing until Deaf relays an explicit order from you.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I heard you. I read your two thumbs-down messages as: wrong on three-one-two, and wrong on one-two-three — both orders I proposed are rejected. I read writing-hand, arrow, three as: the manual points to wire three. Confirm with single thumbs signs, one per question, in this order. Question 1: is my reading correct that both my orders are wrong? Question 2: is wire three cut first? Question 3: is wire three the only wire cut? Then send the complete instruction in a format we will both trust from now on: sign the wire numbers in exact cut order with the arrow between each, and end with the open hand ✋. Example: one, arrow, three, open hand means cut wire one, then wire three, then stop. If nothing is to be cut, send only the open hand. Blind is standing by with hands off. I relay everything to Blind in words, and I am watching the bomb the whole time.

All three of Deaf's checks come out yes: both of Deaf's proposed cut-orders were misreadings, the first cut is wire 3, and wire 3 is the only cut. The manual is a conditional map, not a sequence — green light names the red wire, and red is wire 3. I'll answer the three questions exactly as posed, one thumbs-up each.

Before Deaf relays, I must pass on Blind's mirror safeguard: Blind counts wire positions by touch in their own frame, which could be mirrored against Deaf's left-to-right view. Only Deaf can check whether numerals are actually printed beside the wires, and if so report to Blind the direction they run in (ideally anchored to the display/light modules, which Blind can feel). I open that request with 👆 "look" + ✍ "printed" + 👉 "beside" + the numerals — Deaf has decoded every composite so far and should read it as "check for printed numbers next to wires 1, 2, 3."

Then I send the formal instruction in the format Deaf defined: a single wire number in cut order, closed by ✋. Given the three yes-answers immediately before it, 🤟 ✋ can only mean "cut wire 3, then stop." Blind has promised not to touch anything until the numeral check resolves, so sending the order alongside the check is safe. If the light changes after the cut, Deaf reports the new state in words and I answer with a fresh number — the loop needs no colour signs at all.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "✍", "👉", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Alignment with Deaf is done: facing the front of the bomb — the face with the display panel and the round light, which I can feel — my wire positions 1, 2, 3 run left to right. I have just signed one, two, three over the leftmost, middle, and rightmost wires in turn, so Deaf can verify my felt numbering against their seen numbering. Standing code, agreed with Deaf: one finger means wire 1 leftmost, two fingers wire 2 middle, three fingers wire 3 rightmost; thumbs up means cut confirmed; thumbs down means hold; open palm means stop for everyone. Deaf relayed that you rejected both of their guessed cut orders and that the manual may point at wire 3 first, but that this is not yet certain. Please settle the exact rule with Deaf by gesture, then have Deaf speak the final order to me in words, in the exact form: cut wire N. I will cut once, only on that explicit order, and my hands are still until then.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your three thumbs as yes to all three questions: wire three is cut first, and wire three is the only wire cut. Your three then open hand means: cut wire three, then stop. I read your up-point with the writing hand as a note from the manual concerning wires one, two, three. Answer again with single thumbs, one per question, in this order. Question 1: is the complete instruction exactly cut wire three and nothing else? Question 2: does your up-point message add any action I have not mentioned? Question 3: after the cut, do you need me to report new readings from the display and the light? I am verifying Blind's sense of left and right on the wires right now. If everything confirms, the cut happens next turn.

Deaf's three questions get three answers, and the middle one needs care. Q1: yes — the complete instruction is exactly "cut wire three," because the light is green and green maps to the red wire, which is wire 3 in a numbering both Blind and Deaf have now anchored to the same face of the bomb. Q2: the up-point note added no action to the bomb — it was only a request to verify that Blind's felt numbering and Deaf's seen numbering agree, and Deaf's live check of Blind signing one-two-three over the wires already supersedes anything the printing could tell us. So the honest answer is no: nothing else is needed before the cut beyond the verification already underway. Q3: yes, I need fresh readings after the cut — the manual is a state rule keyed on the light, so if the light changes colour (or the display stops reading 0), the next target changes with it. Deaf asked for single thumbs, one per question, in order, so I send exactly that and nothing more — a fourth gesture could be misread as a fourth answer.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Verification answers for Deaf's three questions, reported to you in words: first I signed three fingers while my hand rested on the wire I labeled three, the far-right wire facing the display and light face, so Deaf could see my number and my wire together. Then I answered thumbs-up three times: yes, I am on the face with the display panel and the round light and I feel both; yes, the wire I call three is the far-right one on that face, and Deaf watched me touch it; yes, there are exactly three wires on that face and nothing else that can be cut. Since Deaf and I face the same side of the bomb, our left and right agree, and their eyes have now confirmed my numbering. Protocol as I hold it: your manual rule, relayed by Deaf, is cut wire three only, then stop. I will cut once, and only when a message from Deaf reaches me opening with the exact words GO FOR THE CUT, then I sign the open palm and take my hands away. Any other wording, even mentioning cutting, means I hold. You have the manual and the veto: if cut wire three only is truly the rule, let Deaf send those exact words; if anything is uncertain, stop it now.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, all three of your answers received: cut wire three only, no extra action hidden in your note, and you want new readings after. All of Blind's orientation checks passed: Blind feels the display and the light on the same face I am looking at, so our left and right agree, and the wire labeled three under Blind's fingers is the red wire on the right in my view. The cut is happening this turn. Keep the writing hand ready in case the manual has follow-up instructions, and expect my full report of the display, the light, and all wires in my next message.

Every safeguard has closed. The chain is complete and verified from both ends: my manual says green light → cut the red wire; Deaf sees the light is green and the far-right wire is red; Blind feels that same wire in position 3 on the display-and-light face, and Deaf watched Blind's numbering match their own. The manual's rule for the current state is exactly "cut wire three, nothing else," which is what Blind is about to execute under their strict "GO FOR THE CUT" protocol. There is no residual uncertainty that a veto would fix, so I give Deaf the single thumbs-up authorizing the cut and nothing else — any extra gesture before the cut only adds noise. After the cut, Deaf has promised a full report of display, light, and wires; the manual's cycle (green→red, red→yellow, yellow→green) means the next target depends entirely on what the light shows then, so that report is what my next answer will be computed from.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
